review_candidates.description: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), based in Geneva, is a humanitarian organization that provides protection and assistance to people affected by armed conflict and other situations of violence. It employs more than 15,000 staff and is present in more than 90 countries. The ICRC Delegation in Maputo is looking for a suitable candidate to fill the following vacancy: WatHab Generalist Project Manager. Purpose: Based in Maputo, reporting to the Focal Point for the Program in favour of People Deprived of Liberty and with the technical support and supervision from the WatHab Coordinator, the Water and Habitat in Detention Engineer plans, designs, and implements engineering projects consistent with the ICRC’s objectives in the field of water and habitat assistance. He/she monitors the progress of the WatHab contribution to the Program in the field, performs needs assessments and studies, implement and plans new projects. He/she works in close cooperation with internal and external partners on the various projects, with a particular focus on providing technical support and mobilizing SERNAP in the establishment of mechanisms ensuring proper operationalization and maintenance of prison infrastructure. Functional Responsibilities: Prepares all project-related documents (forms, maps, books) and necessary material before field assessments. Participates in evaluation missions and prepares full reports of project assessments (proposals); provides design data when required. Collects data required for projects from regional/sectoral authorities and national counterparts. Drafts plans, prepares bills of quantities, and establishes work schedules for projects under his/her responsibility. Prepares project budgets with all required supporting documentation. Supervises project implementation directly and makes the necessary technical decisions. Gathers technical information and periodically reviews project status based on set objectives, keeping the WatHab Coordinator informed. Develops and implements strategies for planning, execution, and monitoring of the Water and Habitat component of the Program in Favour of People Deprived of Liberty as a whole. Establishes a monitoring system for processes and results (creation of periodic monitoring tools for outputs and outcomes of interventions). Analyses the situation in prisons visited by the ICRC and prepares activity and support plans in close collaboration with the Detention team. Works autonomously in needs assessment and ensures proactive and diplomatic progress of processes. Understands issues linked to activities implemented by the delegation and actively contributes to strategy formulation and adjustments. Facilitates the exchange and collection of information related to the security, political, economic, and humanitarian situation in the area of operation. Contributes to security analysis and management in the mission’s area of coverage. Prepares financial needs (cash forecasts) for ongoing or upcoming projects. Conducts project financial monitoring through the Program Assistance Monitoring (PAM) reporting system. Works with the Water and Habitat Coordinator on the consolidation of PAM Progress Reports. Archives all accounting documents related to projects (copies of field expense invoices, payrolls, journals, SRs, etc.). Profile - Minimum required and Experience: University degree in Civil Engineering or Architecture. Minimum 10 years of verifiable post-graduation professional experience in Civil Engineering, Architecture, infrastructure construction, rehabilitation or facilities management. At least five years of demonstrated experience independently managing or technically leading infrastructure projects, including planning, budgeting, procurement, contractor supervision, contract administration, quality control and monitoring. Proven experience in preventive and corrective maintenance, infrastructure condition assessments, rehabilitation planning and operational management of buildings and essential infrastructure. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects, contractors, budgets and implementation schedules with a high degree of technical autonomy. Proven experience working and coordinating with government authorities, public institutions and other institutional stakeholders. Ability to identify infrastructure deficiencies, assess technical and operational risks, prioritize interventions and develop sustainable and cost-effective solutions. Strong technical judgment, analytical thinking, problem-solving skills and demonstrated professional autonomy. Proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with government authorities, penitentiary institutions and senior institutional counterparts. Strong communication, coordination, negotiation and diplomatic skills. Ability to assess complex infrastructure problems and develop practical, sustainable and technically sound solutions. Demonstrated capacity to develop and implement infrastructure maintenance strategies, preventive maintenance programmes and institutional capacity-building initiatives. Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and make sound technical decisions in sensitive operational environments. Strong organizational skills, accountability, professional integrity and results-oriented approach. Proficiency in two languages. English and Portuguese are mandatory. Ability to work within a diverse and multi-cultural team. Ability to manage diverse files in a multi-cultural and regional working environment. Ability to work efficiently across multiple priorities and people. How to apply We are looking for someone methodical, responsible, beneficiary-oriented, with good organizational skills, good sense of teamwork, good communication skills, commitment, initiative and respect for the ICRC's values. We offer dynamic and rewarding work in a humanitarian and multicultural environment, with attractive salaries and social benefits, and opportunities for development through internal training. The ICRC does not ask for any kind of benefit in exchange for a vacancy. The ICRC reserves the right to cancel any application resulting from illegal acts. Please send your application: CV, cover letter, copies of diplomas/certificates by e-mail with the mention in the subject line " WatHab Generalist Project Manager " to: map_recruitment_services@icrc.org Only applications with all the necessary documentation will be considered. Only selected candidates will be contacted. Last day for applications: 6 November 2026 Start Day: earliest possible.

He supports the Head of Mission in relations with donors and partners. Engage new potential donors and partners, working closely with the Head of Mission; Ensure participation in sectoral clusters directly or through figures; DEVELOPMENT Examine the priorities and strategies of the main institutional donors and propose project proposals based on COOPI's expertise and geographical presence; Ensure the final review of all project reports (interim, quarterly and final); Ensure the submission of reports according to internal and external deadlines; Carrying out field monitoring missions in the intervention areas; Supporting the review and approval of MEAL plans for all projects; Using MEAL data to innovate and engage new donors and partners; Human Resources Management Identify human resources needs within existing and/or new programmes; Participate in the staff selection process at the request of the Head of Mission and Headquarters for expatriate and national staff; Train project leaders and other programme staff on monitoring and quality aspects of activities, in coordination with the Head of Mission/Region/Headquarters; Evaluate staff for their part of the competence, according to COOPI procedures; Communication Management and Fund Support production and distribution of communication and visibility tools for COOPI; Collect the necessary data and information in collaboration with field teams to deliver communication products. DESIRED Previous work experience in West, East and Central Africa; Knowledge of the Italian language will be considered a plus. We reserve the right to close the vacancy prior to the application closing date, once a sufficient number of applications has been received. Please note that only the shortlisted candidates will be contacted. COOPI Cooperazione Internazionale is an Italian secular and independent humanitarian organisation fighting against all forms of poverty to improve the world. Founded in 1965, today COOPI is present in 27 countries in Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean and the Middle East, with both emergency and development projects carried out by expatriate staff – an average of over 200 people per year – and national staff. The main institutional funders are the European Union – ECHO and INTPA – USAID, UN agencies, the Italian Government, local authorities and other European Governments. review_candidates.description: About Media.net Media.net is a leading online ad-tech company that develops innovative products for advertisers and publishers. Media.net has one of the most comprehensive portfolios of advertising technology in the industry across search, native, display, mobile, local, products and video. Media.net manages high-quality ad supply on over 500,000 websites and its platform and products are licensed by some of the largest publishers, ad networks and other ad tech companies worldwide. Media.net is one of the largest contextual advertising company worldwide. Media.net has key operation centers across – North America, Europe and Asia. Media.net's US HQ is based in New York, and Global HQ in Dubai. Role Snapshot: Location: Mumbai (Andheri East), India; on-site or hybrid. Shift: US overlap, roughly 6 PM–3 AM IST, with flexibility for US payroll and onboarding peaks. Experience: 4–7 years in Global HR Operations, with at least 2 years supporting US employees. Works With: US employees and managers, third-party payroll/PEO vendor, US benefits and 401(k) providers, India HR and Finance. About the role: This person is the single operational point of contact for our US employees, run from India. They own the US employee lifecycle end to end — onboarding, benefits and 401(k) changes, offboarding — and keep the third-party payroll vendor and our employees in sync. The role executes and coordinates; it does not set US policy or give legal or tax advice. Compliance judgment sits with the payroll vendor and US counsel, and this person knows when to escalate to them. This role will closely work with the CxOs and other POCs from the New York Office on day to day basis Key responsibilities: US onboarding Run new-hire onboarding for US employees: offer-to-day-one checklist, document collection, and system setup with the payroll vendor. Coordinate Form I-9 completion and E-Verify (where used) within federal timelines, plus W-4 and state tax forms. Enrol new hires in benefits and 401(k) within plan eligibility windows; run a first-week orientation on pay, benefits and policies. 401(k) and benefits administration Process 401(k) enrolments, contribution changes, and employer-match updates with the plan provider and payroll vendor. Reconcile payroll deductions against 401(k) remittances each pay cycle and flag mismatches before they become late deposits. Support open enrolment, qualifying life events, and annual plan communications. Offboarding Run exits end to end: final pay on time per state rules, PTO payout, asset and access recovery, and exit interviews. Coordinate COBRA notices, 401(k) separation options, and benefit terminations with the vendor. HR policy Maintain the US employee handbook and policies, keeping them aligned with federal and applicable state requirements. Track US law and benefit changes flagged by the vendor or counsel, and drive the resulting policy updates. Field policy questions and apply policy consistently. Payroll vendor liaison Act as the primary contact for the third-party payroll/PEO vendor: submit inputs (new hires, changes, exits, bonuses) ahead of each cutoff. Review payroll registers before approval and resolve errors with the vendor. Track vendor SLAs and escalate recurring issues. Employee queries and coordination Resolve US employee queries on pay, tax forms, benefits, 401(k) and leave, with a ticket or log for every query. Translate vendor responses into clear answers for employees, and employee issues into clear asks for the vendor. Keep employee records and HRIS data accurate and audit-ready. Must-have qualifications: Graduate; MBA/PGDM in HR preferred. 4–7 years in HR operations, including at least 2 years directly supporting US employees (in-house, GCC, or a US-payroll/PEO outsourcing firm). Hands-on knowledge of US onboarding and exit mechanics: I-9, W-4, state new-hire reporting, final-pay rules, COBRA. Working knowledge of 401(k) administration: enrolment, deferral changes, employer match, and payroll-to-provider reconciliation. Experience managing a payroll or PEO vendor (e.g. ADP, Gusto, Rippling, Justworks, TriNet, Paychex) and reviewing payroll registers. Strong written English for employee-facing communication; comfortable on calls with US staff. Willing to work a sustained US-overlap shift. High discretion with confidential pay and personal data. Good-to-have: SHRM-CP or HRCI (PHR/aPHR) certification. Exposure to multi-state US employment (e.g. California, New York) and state-specific leave rules. Experience with an HRIS such as Workday, BambooHR or Darwinbox, plus a ticketing tool for query tracking. Has written or updated an employee handbook. Advanced Excel for payroll and 401(k) reconciliations. Success in the First 6 Months: Payroll Timeliness: Submit 100% of payroll inputs before the vendor cutoff for every pay cycle. Payroll Accuracy: Maintain zero repeat errors attributable to our inputs. 401(k) Reconciliation: Reconcile deductions against remittances during every pay cycle, with all mismatches resolved within the same cycle. I-9 Compliance: Complete I-9 documentation for 100% of new hires within the federally mandated deadlines. Final Pay Compliance: Ensure 100% of employee exits receive final pay in accordance with applicable state laws. Employee Query Management: Acknowledge employee queries within 1 business day and resolve them within 5 business days. US Employee Handbook: Review and update the US employee handbook by the end of Month 6.
